People were moaning, crying out of the terror, the suffering, all these terrible things that were going on. Because if you started saying something, then they would start shooting in the air, and then you'd bow your head and then you wouldn't dare even look up. And it was only when they would say that you could look up that you did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many armed soldiers were there in room 3 and with what were they armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The armed soldiers were up in the corner before the desk and behind the line-up. I -- on one desk I saw a machine-gun, and the others had automatic rifles. There were about four or five of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How injured, and if so, permanently or otherwise as a result of the beating you received?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my rib was broken on the left-hand side, and I was also hit in the head. That's when I passed out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you then spend four days in this room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we spent a total of three days in that room. Well, no. Yeah, it comes to four days, yes, because in the morning the next day, we were transferred to the other room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of your time in room 3 were people taken out on a selected basis from time to time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From time to time, they were calling out the names of the people who were a bit better off. And then they would sometimes kill them immediately, take them back to room number 1, and then gunshots would be heard. And then the same men were returned and say, you, you, you, and you. They would mention the names of four persons because they needed the corpses to be carried out. I don't know where they carried them. Then they returned these prisoners among us. And then we'd whisper among ourselves and then we'd hear that those other people had been killed and carried out somewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any questioning before the killing of these particular selected detainees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were asking them to confess something, but no one had anything to confess. They were looking for money and gold as I said awhile ago. These were people who were a bit better off. They had shops. They had worked abroad, and they were looking for their money and their gold.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to give the names of some of the people who were taken out and killed from room 3?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Paragraph 31 of the summary, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can mention Hasan Avdic, Ramiz Sinanovic, Nurija Jasarevic, Avdo Jasarevic. I could see them as they were being taken out.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 29. Just yes or no to this, please: Were you also aware of a man being taken out of the building and being taken back to his home village in order that he could find property to hand over to the soldiers? Just yes or no to that at this stage.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the property that he handed over a hunting rifle? Just yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, again I don't think -- the name could be given in private session, and it can be pursued further if anybody needs to. Otherwise, it's not necessary for me to deal with that detail.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 32. Did you see people actually killed in room 3? If so, give us a name or names.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In room number 3, they killed Osman Smajlovic. They said, "Who's the one who builds mosques?" And somebody else said, "This is the one." And then on of them walked up to him and fired a few gunshots into him from a pistol and then he was carried out. They killed a father and a son I think they were who had tried to go elsewhere. They thought that they could go out, but then they returned and then they started shooting from this corner up here, and they killed the two of them as well. I don't know their names though.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many people in all do you calculate were killed in the time that you were at this hangar, the four or five days you were at this hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my free estimate would be about 180 men plus some who were taken to be exchanged allegedly in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me turn to those immediately. Paragraph 33. Was this on the 3rd of June? And just give an explanation of what happened, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they came only once. They said, "We need 25 people to be exchanged in Sarajevo." It wasn't that there was any roll-call. Those who were right by the wire, they simply walked out. And I saw among them Ismet Ahmetovic from Klisa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Has he ever been accounted for since?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: None of them have ever been accounted for since.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your time in room 3, did you learn what shifts the soldiers were working and get something about the number of soldiers per shift?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they had three shifts consisting of eight soldiers respectively.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What, if any, provision of food was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes they would throw in a few loaves of bread among us. And then when people would manage to grab a bit, they would eat it. They would also throw in some tins, but then we had nothing to open the tins with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 36. May we go into private session for just a couple of sentences, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So far as you were concerned, Witness B-1098, were all the guards present in the hangars involved in the killings of people there or only some or can't you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think all of them were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 5th of June, did the guards inform you that your position was to change? If so, what did they tell you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They told us that we were going and that some buses would be arriving shortly and that we would be taken for an exchange by Odzak way. I'd never been to Odzaci myself but that's where they said we were going. We never arrived in Odzaci. We arrived in Pilica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Odzak is a village I think in the direction of Brcko? And the --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the buses on which you travelled were the buses of which firm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The buses belonged to the Drinatrans firm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got to Pilica, the Chamber will be already familiar with this, it's at the top part of the map and it actually marked as Donja Pilica. When you got to Pilica, what happened there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the buses were stopped there because that centre is on the left-hand side. They stopped the buses and we moved round about where there was a door. You had to go right the way round to the door there. And then those that remained alive, we were all pushed into that hall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you guarded? What were the uniforms of those guarding you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is how it was: Nobody actually guarded us there. The doors were shut, and just the holes where you could see the film. And somebody would come in from there or throw in something. They would throw actually loaves of bread and tins through that hole where the camera sometimes was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they say anything as they looked at you through that hole or threw food for you through that hole?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all I remember is that a woman said that if her brother were killed, she would kill all of us. She threatened us from up there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What was the building that they were put into? Can you explore that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: My error for not making it clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the building into which you were placed in Pilica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a cinema hall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what you've been describing as the place through which they threw bread was the projection room or something like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before we -- before we move on, would the Chamber be good enough to turn to tab 4 of Exhibit 456, which is a record of the Drinatrans coach company. The witness has the original to view, and indeed there's nothing to stop its going on the overhead projector to reveal the sort of records that were kept of what was being done. It's on the Sanction. Thank you very much. There are two entries we're going to be looking at on this, but the first one is for the 3rd of June where it refers to Zvornik-Djulici and back, settling of refugees. And although -- sorry. And then the next -- and then the 5th of June we see Zvornik-Djulici and back, settling of refugees. On the 5th of June. And then we see the 5th of June, Zvornik-Pilica and back, transport of prisoners. Can you comment on the consistency of these entries, which of course you haven't seen until recently, with the movement you've described, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what you mentioned on the 3rd of June, Zvornik-Djulici and vice versa, these could only be refugees from Brnci, from Zivinice. Then the 5th of June, Zvornik-Djulici and back and the settling of refugees, that mean the same. It was just that they settled in stages. And as for the 5th of June, Zvornik-Pilica, that entry, that was us, those of us who were taken to Pilica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 43. On the 3rd day of your detention in Pilica, did the guards come and tell you that your condition was to change again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did they tell you, and what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what happened was that they opened the door and told us to line up and form a column moving towards the back of the hall and that we should come forward one by one. The truck was waiting outside, and there was a table, a desk at which a man was sitting writing the names and surnames and our father's names as well. He was entering the names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was it said was going to happen to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They said we'd be going to Zivinice for the exchange?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: How many men boarded this truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I got into the first truck and I was among the last. And I know that when he completed the list there were 64 of us, and he said, "That's enough. 64 is sufficient."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it preferable that the names the witness can give at the end of paragraph 44 be given in private session with your leave.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the tarpaulin on this truck, which I think was a two-tonne civilian truck, pulled down and did the truck drive back in the direction of Karakaj and nowhere near the place where you could have expected to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's the same direction from Karakaj towards Zivinice the truck was a two-tonne truck. That's how I call it. I don't know what others call it. And it had a tarpaulin covering the top. And they had fastened the belts and we stayed in the truck. But there was a sort of hole through which they failed to pass this belt. And you could see through the hole. The person that was down there could look through the hole. So we knew the direction we were going in.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, my understanding is that Zivinice is off to the left of the map, and if -- I didn't mean to mislead the witness. Maybe the first part of the journey would have gone in the same direction, but it's a matter of detail and we'll move on to what happened at Karakaj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: En route to Karakaj was the truck escorted, and if so by what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was escorted by the police with that rotating light that they have on top.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Back at Karakaj, were you brought to the same area that you had been in before at the technical school?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Tab 5 for the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The same general area. Not to the same precise place, the same general area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Brought to Karakaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And if Your Honours look at tab 5, again the original must be under seal. A redacted version is being displayed by computer system on the screens at the moment, and the orientation is different again by 90 degrees, but the Chamber will recognise the configuration of roads on the right-hand side of this map with the configuration of roads on the top left-hand side of tab 3 if it needs to match one to the other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got to Karakaj, to what building did the truck take you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It took us to Gero's slaughterhouse. After I escaped, that's what I learnt from those people. When I describe where we were, they said that's what it was called, Gero's slaughterhouse.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this plan of yours, our Exhibit 456, tab 5, shows it as being on the opposite side of the road from the technical school hangar and beside the garages of the transport company or coach company Drinatrans; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On arrival, how close to the building was the lorry parked, and describe the method by which the tarpaulin was adjusted so that the 64 of you could be moved from the lorry into the building.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When they wanted to park the lorry, they reversed it towards the doors of the building, and then one of the people that had been captured said, "Well, take all the killed outside." And they put the -- drove the truck up to the doorway. They looped the ropes through the tarpaulin, and you had to jump out. And as you jumped out, you were straight into the hall. So one group had to go to the right. The rest had to go to the left. And I don't know whether they put anybody into the premises that were further away, but I was in the right-hand side of the hall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Jumping out in that way directly into the building, the plan of which we'll see in a second, did that mean you had no or no substantial view of the area immediately outside the building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you learn by one means or another that the -- both from yourself and also from other things you may have been told or seen at the time, did you learn of what was in fact outside the building from which you were kept by being funneled into the building directly from the tarpaulin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said a moment ago that the people were killed while the truck was reversing towards the building. One of the soldiers said, "Everybody out," and they were all shot. And that's how we realised that we would be killed too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you mark the slaughterhouse on the plan as A, recording the fact that it's close to a Muslim settlement; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we turn now to Exhibit 456, tab 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we turn to Exhibit 456, tab 6. Again, the original exhibit under seal, a redacted version being displayed. And if we look at the left-hand part of this sketch, does that show an end view of the building with the door into which you were funneled with below it a concrete fence or wall? On the right-hand side does it show the inside of -- the inside plan of the building going through the door in the middle of the bottom of that little oblong with two rooms, room 1 on the right as you've described it, and room 2 on the left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you went into room 1, tell us what happened and please give the description of any uniform of the soldiers who were involved.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went into room 1. The rest went into the -- into room 2. I -- as I said, I don't know if anybody went into room A. And suddenly they said, "Turn your heads toward the wall," which we did. And then a burst of gunfire started. People fell down. I was -- I also fell down. And then they killed the others in the other rooms or, rather, in room number 2. I know that in room 1 there was a man who was wounded in the lower extremity of his body. He entreated them to kill him, but they didn't want to. One shouted out and said, "I've got enough ammunition. Why don't you kill him?" And the other one said, "I don't want to shoot. Let the balija suffer." I was still conscious then, and I heard this exchange between these two men. As far as the uniforms are concerned, it was a soldier. He was 19 or 20 years old, a nice looking young man. He was a soldier of the Yugoslav People's Army. He had curly hair. He might have been 170 -- to 170 centimetres tall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice indeed his cap and what markings he had on his cap?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did wear a cap. The normal cap worn by the Yugoslav People's Army with a star on it at the forehead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Can we have it clarified as to who this man is?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The man you're describing as a guard in this room, was he a man who did any of the killing or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who do you mean by the guard? I didn't quite understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The guard you've just described.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they weren't guards. They just brought us there to kill us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so to answer His Honour's question --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as we were --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To answer His Honour's question, the man you've described, the young man, curly hair and the cap with the star, what did he do? Did he engage in the killing himself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he personally killed these people down there. As to the others, I don't know who killed them, but I know he killed the group that I was in because he came in the door. Our backs were turned -- we were facing him first of all and then he ordered us to face the wall. And that's how I happen to remember him, and he's in my memory still.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You fell down but in fact had not been shot; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hadn't been hit then, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to hear what happened in room 2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I heard was groaning and moaning and crying. That's all I heard. And of course the shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the remark that you told us about of the guard who declined to kill the balija who -- the man he described as a balija saying he should suffer, what did the guards do? Where did they go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I was still conscious, I could hear everything they were saying. They said, "Switch the motor on and we're going to get next lot." So they switched the engines on of the truck and they went off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you check your surroundings to see if there was anybody else left behind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said a moment ago that the person that entreated the people to kill him, he just made a motion. He didn't say anything, but he just asked me, indicating with his head, "Where are you going?" And I just told him that I was going outside. I went into the hall. There was nobody around. There was just a concrete wall. I had to pass through a wheat field and went beyond that into a meadow and some high grass where I hid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On your way from the building and across the wall, were you able to see if there were bodies around?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And remind us, your truck of people who went into the building was the first truck to come from the cinema hall where you'd been detained?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Escaping across the wall and being able to hide yourself in a meadow, did you see or hear the same truck coming back on one or more subsequent occasions to this building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They came back two more times in the course of the day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On each of those occasions, what did you see or hear of what they did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just heard bursts of gunfire in that same building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the basis that the same number of people were in the lorry on each occasion, your calculation is that how many people were brought there for killing in the course of this particular day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, 64 would make it 192.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If that figure is right for those or approximately right for those brought to this building for killing, that would have left on your calculation approximately how many people in the cinema hall in Pilica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 300.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, have those people ever been accounted for since?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard some not too reliable information that they had been killed by Branjevo way. And this was on the 11th of June for the Muslim holiday Bajram.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Included in the people left behind at the cinema hall in Pilica, were there, just yes or no to this, relations of yours, your brother and your father?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Assuming that the lorries coming back -- the lorry coming back on the two occasions was bringing people from the cinema hall, you're not in a position to say one way or another whether your brother and father would have been on the lorry on either of those two occasions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But is the position this: That your father and brother have not been accounted for since?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. They have not been accounted for. We don't know what happened to any of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you learn of one other man who it was said had survived presence at an attack in the slaughterhouse? If so, what was his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One in the third group survived. However, he was killed during the war. And his name is Vejsil Hamzic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 54. We may be able to take this part of your history comparatively briefly, B-1098, did you leave the area of your hiding and walk north, seeing peeking working in the fields so that you hid by day and moved by night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went along the Drina River, and I got closer to the bridge across which the trains go to Serbia, but there were guards up there on the bridge, so that I hid in the bushes and waited for darkness to fall. And when night fell, I crossed the rail tracks where they were on the ground, and I headed towards where the Sapna River flows into the Drina River. And from there --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Pausing there for a minute because we don't need to pursue the geography of your movements too closely, but at that junction of the two rivers, did you notice a tank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I was wandering around in the night, I came across a kind of kiosk. It was lit up, and I got to ten metres from the tank. When I noticed it, I moved off towards the left. And when I got close to the river, I saw a body. It was dressed in jeans, top and bottom. It was lying down. I fled from there and hid in a haystack. It was almost dawn by then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spent a day in a haystack, camouflaged, and in the course of that day did you see on several occasions a man who came with different people but to whom that man gave the same account?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see him because I was hiding in the hay. I just left a hole to be able to breathe. And then two or three or four times he was bringing some people, and I remember the name. Sane. Look where I was and look where he is. I shot him and killed him. And this one said, "Why didn't you slit his throat?" And he said, "When I got there, he was dead so why would I do that?"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of your movements did you find yourself walking some degree in circles so that you came back near to the spot where you had so nearly been executed yourself? Did you hide there and did you notice two vehicles in the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: True enough. I got lost during the night thinking that I had reached the Sapna. In fact, I had gone back towards of the path to Kozluk. So I got close to the same place where I was actually executed or an attempt was made to execute me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the two vehicles you saw there were what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A loader and a lorry parked there. And just then I noticed them putting the tarpaulin across the sides, not over the top. So I assume that they were loading bodies. Now, where they drove them to, I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the vehicle that you describe as a loader, was that something that had a mechanism that could load or move a substantial amount of earth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can push the ground, raise it up, and unload it onto a truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By your calculation, the date on which you saw this loader and the lorry with the tarpaulin would be what? What day in June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be the 10th of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you then move to a nearby bridge where you hid in a bush, and from that position were you able to hear some soldiers who were with a dog, but did you hear the soldiers discussing Muslim men and women?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true. I hid in the same place I had hid in the first time, and again I waited for night to fall. I saw two soldiers. The bridge was lit up. I couldn't pass across the water or the bridge. There were lights everywhere. And I saw two soldiers leading a dog on a leash, and I heard their conversation. One said, "You should see how many Muslim men and women they have brought. We will have plenty." I don't want to use the word that they used regarding the women, but that's what they meant. "We'll have plenty to you know what."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you spend that night in a forest and the following day find yourself in formerly Muslim territory that had been cleansed, as it is described, so that you thought it comparatively safe to be walking there, and then did you find yourself in an opening in the forest in sight of two men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you surrender to those two men because they required you to do so, and where did they take you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There may be an error there. I was caught by one, but I saw two others on a clearing. I was hiding from those two, and I went through the forest. How I didn't look carefully, and this man had a gun. He said, "Hands up." And I did, and then he took me to these other two up there. And there were three women with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the event you were able to escape from them by throwing a bag you had at them and running away; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time you did that, had one of the men left to make contact with a local organisation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was like a small radio station or a Motorola, and he couldn't reach the Crisis Staff from there so he had to climb up to a little hill. And I asked him to release me. And when he left and I asked them to let me go, but they wouldn't. I threw the bag at them, and I ran away about 300 or 500 metres, and only then I heard two or three shots, but they weren't close by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know which particular Crisis Staff he was going to contact or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Celopek.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You moved on from this area, paragraph 60, and there came a time when you saw two Serbian soldiers near to you, I think.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true. I was hungry. I hadn't eaten for days. I climbed a cherry tree to pick up cherries. The village had been cleansed from Muslims. I thought there was no one there. So I was more relaxed knowing the area. And I was eating these cherries, and I heard a branch break. I turned around and saw two men in camouflage uniforms. I jumped up, and they shot at me and they wounded me. Nevertheless, I ran into a stream. I turned right, then I turned back towards them again but not using the same route but in that same direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And eventually to cut this story short, eventually you were able to reach free territory and ultimately to be treated for the bullet wound you'd sustained, in the Tuzla hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These two couldn't find me though they wanted badly to slaughter me, but thank God I managed to reach free territory, and I was in Tuzla undergoing treatment for a month.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You will be asked some further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, do you have any evidence coming as to whether those people who were shot in the room with the witness as to whether their bodies were recovered and any forensic evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Just one minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I think Your Honour's question is directed to that category of evidence we've had elsewhere where mass graves can be connected or might sometimes be connected to the evidence of killings of this kind, and the answer to that question is not yet, but there are further inquiries under way at the moment. There is another witness who can also deal not in that way but in another way with this particular execution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Because in my view, the method of killing is a matter for consideration in relation to the crime. I want to ask the witness. Witness, can you tell me, you fell unconscious. You were not shot, but had you been hit by a bullet? Am I to take it you had been hit in the back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wasn't hit anywhere at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No. Yes, I know you were not hit, but had you been hit, can you say where you would have been hit? Would you have been hit in the back part of your body or on the front? Because earlier you said that you were all told to line up and to face the wall, and I believe Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. you also said that as soon as your backs were towards the guards, they started shooting. So what I want to find out is when the shots were fired, where were you facing? Were you facing the wall along with the other men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was facing the wall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think that's as much as I can get. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Cross-examination after the adjournment. Twenty minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, you have one hour and a half to examine this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not sure that that will be sufficient for me, but we'll see later on, Mr. May. Cross-examined by Mr. Milosevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. 1098, let us begin with where you stopped and then we'll go back to the beginning of your testimony. A moment ago, you explained to Mr. Robinson that you were all facing the wall, that they had ordered you to face the wall; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you lined up in a row and all of you facing the wall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everyone was facing the wall, all around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe that for me, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I described it when I said that we were lined up against the wall and we were told to face the wall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there was a total of 64 of you that had got there, so about half of you were in that room; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, approximately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So around 32 of you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the third room. I said a moment ago I don't know how many people were in that third room. I can't say how many of us were in the room I was in exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many soldiers entered in that room with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not a single one of them. They were at the door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Fine. Will you please be kind enough and provide the sketch on the ELMO, the sketch drawn by this witness with those two rooms that the alleged execution took place in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Tab 6, I think.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Place it on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Your Honour, microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. It can't go on the ELMO, but it can go on the Sanction and we can have it on our screens. It's on there now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not that sketch, the bigger one showing the two rooms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Nice, can you help as to what the accused is talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I think it's tab 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Tab 3. Right. Try tab 3.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. There's a room on the right and another one on the left. I remembered it from the ELMO. That is not the sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Tab 6 then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. That's the one. That's the one where the crime took place. The other one was of Karakaj and where he was detained.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was showing the sketch of the building that he called Gero's slaughterhouse, and on the ELMO there was a sketch showing those rooms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: There it is. If you -- look on the screen and you'll see it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is apparently -- A must be the rooms to the left and the right; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please magnify that sketch? Enlarge it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, will you please look at that sketch. You were in room number 1.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's a room 3 by 3 metres; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, explain to me, how is it possible that in a room 3 by 3, 30 and more men can be lined up against the wall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, Mr. Milosevic, I described it differently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you describe it? Would you be kind enough to tell me, because I assume if a room is 3 metres long and 3 metres wide and you say some 30 men were lined up against the wall, how is it possible to put so many people in that room which is 3 by 3?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that one group went to room number 1, and I was there too, and the others went to the room to the left. How many went up there, I said I didn't know, in room marked A.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What you are saying is impossible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That there were about 30 of you in that room. Were there 30 of you in that room or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't count them, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't count them, but a moment ago you answered my question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't answer in the way you put it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Then explain to me, please, since what you said or drew here was impossible, did you draw these sketches?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you wrote in the words in English?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just drew it out first. Now, who drew it in in English, I don't know. I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you just drew the lines, and the words were written by someone else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "3 by 3," and "number 1," and "3 by 3," "number 2," and the "Corridor," I did I it but in Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So you were executed in that room with a group of some 30 men. Then you explained that you fled from there because when the soldiers left, no one was guarding the building. There were no men around there, were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were only dead people outside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But no guards or anyone else. It was abandoned because they went to fetch some others; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They turned on the engine of the truck. I heard them do that and say, "We're going to get the next lot." And when I was leaving, there were no guards there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And then you watched behind the wall as they brought the truck back twice.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say behind the wall. I said from the spot where I was hiding.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you saw the truck coming back twice repeating the same procedure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The truck came twice, and bursts of fire could be heard twice again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, in the meantime as there was no one there, it means that they used this same room three times, a room 3 by 3, brought some other men in there. So in the end, about a hundred people were executed in that same room 3 by 3?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily. They could have executed them outside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you said that the same procedure was repeated.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never said that they were brought into the room. I just heard the truck arrive, and I heard bursts of fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You say that now. A moment ago, you put it differently. Tell me, please, you were in the first truck and then they brought two more trucks. This truck that you say 64 of you were brought in; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you yourself said, it was a two-tonne truck.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you realise that it is absolutely not possible to put 64 men into a two-tonne truck even if they were sitting on each other's heads? Do you know what a two-tonne carrying capacity is? You know how much space it has, to put in two cubic metres of goods on it? Why did you make that up? Tell me, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why don't you ask me a specific question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My specific question to you is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What is the point of it? Just a moment. What sort of a truck it was, does it really matter? We are dealing with immensely serious events here. The massacre of hundreds of people, and whether they went into a two-tonne or three-tonne truck really cannot matter. This sort of detail does not assist. I mean, you're not suggesting, are you, that this witness made this up?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, you cannot put a litre of water into this glass. As for a two-tonne truck which has its own dimensions that are easy to establish, it is simply impossible to board 64 men onto that kind of a truck. That's what I'm saying, because I'm saying that this witness did invent what he said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's proceed. Did you say that they took everything away from you the first time and then that the next time they were trying to take everything away from you so they took everything away from you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Milosevic, even my wife and children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't have anything with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing. Nothing, absolutely. They separated my wife and children, and they executed me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But since they took everything away from you twice, how come you had a bag in your hands ultimately, that you threw away -- that you threw at these people so that you would frighten them and then you could run away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not a bag. It's a mere shopping bag, a plastic shopping bag. I found it in Karakaj. I put my shoes and my jacket into that plastic shopping bag and I carried it with me. It was raining at the time so I wanted to change my shoes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To change your shoes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I wore these big rough shoes because my feet were wet because of the rain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I understand that you didn't have anything on you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that down there in Karakaj, in a house, I found -- in a Muslim house I found a jacket and these rough boots and that's what I wore. And I put my own shoes into this plastic bag.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 2, paragraph 4 of your statement, you say that as a worker, you were employed in a Belgrade company, or rather, two.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two. But I don't want to mention them here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is the period of 1975 to 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that was all of 17 years?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You worked in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in Belgrade. Well, not all of it was if Belgrade. Some of this time was in Russia.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the accused.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Practically for 17 years you stayed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We're being asked to slow down so that the microphone could be operated. Could you, both of you, wait until the other has finished. And if the witness would make sure not to speak before the accused's microphone has gone off. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spent 17 years in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, throughout this time as you worked in Belgrade companies during those 17 years, did you have any problem whatsoever because you were a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say on page 2 in paragraph 6 that when the war started you came from Belgrade to your village. I'm not going to refer to the name of the village because this question was dealt with in closed session at the very beginning of this hearing. And you came to celebrate Bajram; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you come to the village exactly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was the 3rd of April. Approximately the 3rd of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So you did not return from Belgrade because the war had broken out. You went there to celebrate Bajram with your family; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that I came to celebrate Bajram.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that the reason for your departure from Belgrade was that you were going home for a few days to celebrate Bajram and that's what you told your superiors at work; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in the company, we never said that. This happened to be a Thursday and Friday, I think. So that's how we went home over the weekend.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said, "I'm going home for the holiday now"; right? For Bajram. And that was the reason, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said just awhile ago during the weekend. Every weekend practically we went home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody make problems for you in this respect if you wanted to go home and celebrate the holiday, things like that? Did people object in any way to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Objections were made on the day when we left Belgrade, Mr. Milosevic. Buses were returned from the customs on the highway. They were returned to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were returned from the customs on the highway, and we returned to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't notice that. How did you manage to leave then if you left -- if you had to go back to Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We found a Lasta company bus and went via Obrenovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Tell me, since you claim that you returned when the war broke out, your neighbours, your Serb neighbours, warned you that the situation was becoming dangerous as far as I can see from this statement of yours. On the basis of these warnings that the situation was becoming dangerous, you went to Klisa; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This actually means that then when you went towards Klisa, in your village there were no conflicts and no war operations at that time; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was shooting. There was individual gunfire, but not in the village itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who are these local Serbs who warned you about this danger, that there was some kind of danger? Can you tell us that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you want, we could go into private session to do that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, only if he knows how to answer this question. If he can't answer it, then there's no need to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that I've already said this once.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 2, in paragraph 6 you say, "Most of the Muslims from my village fled to Klisa. Among others, my family and I." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me now, since your Serb neighbours warned you that there was some kind of danger, you actually heeded this warning and you left the village. You didn't have to flee before anyone; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, we were told to take cars and to take some food, and whoever had a tractor or any other kind of vehicle, to get food and to go to Klisa because the UNHCR and the Red Cross would come and accompany us to Medjedje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, did anybody expel you from your village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as soon as this order was issued, it means that we were expelled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My impression was that somebody told you that there was some kind of danger, and you didn't check this. You simply left. It's not that somebody came and said, "Now, leave the village."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, but we were told that we would get killed because some paramilitary units had come.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I didn't notice that in your statement either, so I cannot establish how it was that you left your village. You claim that on the 1st of June, 1992, to your total astonishment you realised that the paramilitary units and the JNA had totally surrounded the village of Klisa and that had you known that, as you say, you would have tried to escape to free territory, as you had put it, rather than waiting for the Chetniks to come and capture you. Is that what you stated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said a short while ago that we were told that the UNHCR and the Red Cross would come. However, it is true that the Chetniks came and surrounded the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. First of all, tell me who are these Chetniks? Do you mean by that word the members of a particular formation or is this the way that you are referring to the local Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean everybody who killed innocent people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Please, on page 3 in paragraph 1, you explain who was who, and this is what you say, I am quoting you: "I think that soldiers in olive-grey uniforms were members of the regular forces of the JNA and soldiers in camouflage uniform were local Chetniks." Is that what you stated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to tell you the truth, I called both Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, all Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not all Serbs. There are good Serbs too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, there are good Serbs. But in the preceding statement -- sentence in the statement quoted to you, you say that you did not recognise a single soldier, any member of the paramilitary formations, but nevertheless, you say that Chetniks in camouflage uniforms were local people.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I claim that because they were wearing masks on their faces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on that basis you came to the conclusion that they were locals?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely. That's why I came to that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did your locals get these masks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't only masks. There were plain socks too, the ones that had slits for the eyes only, black ones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you say they were members of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what I claim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I can see from your statement that you also did your compulsory military service in the JNA, and it was even more than ten years before all of this; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is right. I did my military service in the JNA, but I served in Tito's army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in that year, in 1992, you were also a reservist of the JNA, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was never called up in the reserve force, and I never had an assignment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't have an assignment but you know that others who, for example, did have an assignment, who were Muslims just like you, that at home they had these same olive-grey uniforms that had been issued to them, and they had them at home, the same uniform like the JNA had. Is that right or is that not right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm just speaking in my own name. And who was issued with what, I don't know. I just know that the police had automatic weapons and that they were taken away from them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know that reservists had these uniforms that were quite the same, that they were the same like the JNA uniforms, reservists in Yugoslavia before the war broke out regardless whether they're Serbs, Muslims, Slovenians, Macedonians? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I know that the uniforms were the same before the war broke out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the basis of what are you saying then that members -- that people in olive-grey uniforms were members of the JNA if they could have been territorials or reservists or anybody else who had that kind of uniform or who had been issued with that kind of uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I claim that because these were very young men, youths.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the other hand, there weren't any youths in the army of Republika Srpska and the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina? Did these armies consist of elderly men only?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina did not even exist, I think. There was only the Yugoslav People's Army along with the reserve force as you mentioned it awhile ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, these events that you testify about, when did they happen? The beginning of June; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true, yes, the beginning of June. On the 1st of June, not the beginning of June. The 1st.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned dates between the 1st and 10th of June. That is the time period about which you are testifying; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I refer to the time between the 1st and 12th of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 1st to the 12th of June. And do you know that the JNA along with its units left the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina by the 19th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. In response to one of my previous questions, you said, as you had stated, that you would have escaped from Klisa and gone to free territory as you had put it had you known that instead of the Red Cross and the UNHCR it would be the Serb forces that would come in; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that I would have fled, but there was a roadblock down there. From Klisa quite a few people managed to flee through the woods into free territory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Tell me, what was this free territory in 1992 at that time, now that you've called it the free territory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I call it the free territory, and by this I mean the territory where these paramilitary formations did not come, and I don't believe that these paramilitaries or the army, not only Seselj's men, Arkan's men, but only where people were defending themselves, when they realised what was going on in other parts of the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And who controlled the territory that you refer to as the free territory? In the military sense of the word, who controlled it, this free territory of yours, the one you refer to as the free territory? In the military sense and all other senses, who held it under their control?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That territory was held by the locals of the other villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The locals, the local inhabitants? Is that it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And when you say free territory, do you mean territory without Serbs? Is that it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never said that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But you as a Muslim who spent 17 years in Belgrade went home to celebrate the Bajram holiday and not because of the war, we've established all that, that's what you've said, and now you refer to free territory, which means territory under Muslim control. Is that what you mean when you say "free territory"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I said that I arrived on the 3rd of April and there was no Bosnia -- no war in Bosnia at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you came to the free territory after that. That's why I'm asking you. That's what you say.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I used the term "free territory" in order to denote the regions the locals put up a resistance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And do you know of a single place in Podrinje, I mean Podrinje in Bosnia-Herzegovina. I'm not thinking about Podrinje in Serbia. So do you know of a single place in Podrinje where there were no Serbs, in which Serbs were not residents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat that question, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Podrinje, in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina, is there a single place without Serbs living in it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there are quite a few places, actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean individual villages?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, individual villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, please. Does that mean that the Serbs from that so-called free territory were expelled to some other territory by someone who -- which was free territory for them, just like this territory was Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. free territory for you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who expelled them, I don't know. But, yes, it's true that that did exist too. I wasn't there then. I was being executed at the time, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, tell me, who could have expelled them from that territory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said a moment ago that I don't know because I was in the camp, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You were talking about the fact that the Serb refugees from the Zivinice area had for the most part come to your region, those who had fled from the Zivinice area. So what did they flee from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You would have to ask somebody from Zivinice that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Then tell me, please, and I'm talking about your personal experience, you mentioned Zivinice, the Serb refugees from Zivinice and so on and so forth. Is it true that it was due to these conflicts in that civil war that the Serbs and Muslims, so both the Serbs and the Muslims, in an effort to save their lives and parts of their property would go to neighbouring territory, whether it be near or far, territory which was under the control of their compatriots? That's right, isn't it? That's your experience and quite obviously it's also the experience of the other refugees that you mentioned. You mention the refugees from Zivinice in this case.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't in Zivinice at that time, but I know 100 per cent that the same people from Brnci to Zivinice came to settle in these villages, Bijeli Potok, Lupe [phoen], Tulici and the other surrounding neighbouring villages. So nobody captured them there or killed them either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they fled from those parts, did they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how they happened to come. I don't know how they came to be there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You don't know, but I I'm sure you can assume that was the reason. There can't be any other reason. But as you're talking about -- as you're quoting figures, do you happen to know this, for example: You're talking about your own village. [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can we redact the identifying number of the villages? It's an identifying character, probably too precise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We will go into private session for this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 3, paragraph 2, you state the following: You claim that in Klisa, on the 1st of June, there were about 4.000 Muslim refugees there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that in Klisa, which is predominantly Muslim, according to the population census I quoted a moment ago there were 615 Muslim, which makes it a very small place; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how many, but quite possibly it is that figure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the village of Djulici, once again a predominantly Muslim village there were 1.029, a total of 1.029 inhabitants which doesn't mean that all of them were there at that time. Some were abroad. Some were in different various other places. As you know, the population census incorporates all the inhabitants, the residents regardless of whether they are actually residing there at the time. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, what I'm going to tell you is this: In Klisa, from 13 Muslim villages, refugees were stationed there, and you don't have that piece of information for all the villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I don't have information for all the villages but where do you get this figure of 4.000 from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the people were counted when they came into Klisa, and we knew how many people were in Klisa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the people counted them, did they? You heard that from somebody, that the figure was 4.000? You didn't count them yourself, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had I been in charge, perhaps I would have counted them, but I didn't. Others did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you heard this figure and piece of information from them. That's who you got it from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also say that none of you who had taken shelter in Klisa, none the people there had any weapons, not even those Muslims who lived in Klisa. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the people who happened to find themselves in Klisa had weapons. Had somebody had weapons with them, they would have shot at somebody.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you claim that it was the Serbs who shot in the air, and you say they terrorised you but that this shooting didn't last long and that nobody was wounded as a result; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. I said they shot up into the air. They surrounded Klisa. The tanks arrived in Klisa. There were a lot of soldiers round about, and it's also true that I heard later on once I had escaped that two people were killed in Klisa, that is to say an elderly man and woman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Is the opposite true, though, that in Klisa and the surrounding parts that there was fighting on that particular day, that there were battles and an exchange of gunfire to use that mildest of terms, an exchange of gunfire? Let me put it that way. Is that correct? And that the members of the Muslim formations, I mean armed Muslims when I say paramilitaries, they succeeded in fleeing from Klisa, in escaping in Klisa precisely during that period of time, the one that you're describing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps your information is incorrect. I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could that be the reason for which the Serbs searched for weapons, why they conducted a weapons search?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't conduct a weapons search. They came to loot and pilfer and to destroy the houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you said a moment ago that when you had been captured that they took one man home for him to hand over the weapons he had in his house. So the purpose of the investigation that was conducted was to confiscate the weapons that were used to fire at and for which people were killed -- through which people were killed. Do you know that? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I said quite clearly that one man was taken off. He was a hunter. He had a licence to carry his hunting rifle, and he didn't want to give it up, to surrender it. And the locals knew very well who surrendered their weapons and who did not. So they took him home and brought him back to us, to our group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. They took him home for him to give up his weapon. So the purpose of that entire undertaking was to uncover arms, the weapons that people had who had been detained; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose was -- well, you can go on saying that, but that's not true. They took innocent people off and killed them, Milosevic. That's what they did, killed them down there, not in a search for weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, where is the sense of what you quoted then, that somebody said it would be better for you to own up, to confess? What did they want you to confess? Do you know how many crimes had been committed up until the beginning of June against Serbs in the area, how many Serbs were killed? So what did they want you to confess? They didn't want you to confess your names or anything like that. What did they want you to confess to, to own up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those regions, Mr. Milosevic, handed over the weapons they had. It was not a fighting area. It was sorted of bypassed. They went elsewhere. But we lived there without any fighting. They fought in the villages further up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I heard you say that there was fighting above your villages. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there was fighting. Battles were waged. And now I'm quoting you again. You said that: "One of the Serbs who was there asked whether -- whether there was anybody from Kovacevici among the detainees." Is that right? I'm quoting you on that point. You said someone asked us whether there was anybody from the village of Kovacevici among the detainees. Is that right? You yourself said that, you were quoting a Serb solder as having asked that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true, and I said that there was fighting in Kovacevici, the village of Kovacevici, and this particular man had been wounded in the leg and he wanted to see whether there was anybody from Kovacevici so he could slit their throats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I don't know about that, but he asked whether any of the detainees were from Kovacevici; is that right? Those were your very words; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they were detainees, prisoners captured during that fighting? Isn't that so, Mr. 1098?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, that is completely incorrect. What you're talking about is very far from the villages. These were loyal citizens of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I assume that when he looked among the detainees, the prisoners, then there were prisoners. They weren't civilians?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He's answered it. He said they were civilians.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I was quoting him, Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just -- we've heard his evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. 1098, on that particular day, who captured you and took you to the hangar in Karakaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want me to go back and say it. The JNA, the locals with the masks on their faces so I wouldn't recognise them, people wearing uniforms, those were the ones who captured us, not only myself but the 700 of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the JNA wasn't there at all at that time, but you can continue claiming that if you like. Now, tell me, on page 3, paragraph 7 and also this morning, you said the following: You were transported in three civilian trucks. That's right. That's what you said, isn't it? Is that right?
