utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in these three trucks, 750 of you were transported; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I just saw three trucks. Now, how many people were transferred and whether more trucks turned up, I don't know that, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. 1098, that's what you said. So that's why I'm asking you. If we had three trucks with 250 people in one truck, does that seem to you to be a little improbable or not, regardless of the size of the truck?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He's just answered that. He said there might have been other trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Physically that is impossible, but are you claiming from the standpoint of what you said that there were three civilian trucks, do you believe that members of the JNA used civilian lorries, that the JNA uses civilian lorries?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who sent them, whether it was the JNA that gave that order or maybe the head of Zvornik municipality. I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm glad to hear you don't know that, because actually, up until the 1st of June, you hadn't seen a single JNA member in Klisa, in Djulici or even in Karakaj because the JNA wasn't there at that time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We've been over this. If you want to add anything, B-1098, you can.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to answer this question, if I may. I never claimed that the JNA wasn't in Klisa or Djulici and Karakaj. I said that they were in all three of those places.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm claiming that you made that up and I'm trying to prove that. But you keep saying it was the JNA were there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can say that if you will. You were the person issuing orders, so you may know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, on page 3, fifth paragraph, you say that a total of 750 men were brought to Karakaj on that occasion. And later on on page 4, in paragraphs 4 and 6, say you were all shut up in two small rooms.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's quite so. Seven hundred of us. One was small and another -- the other room was bigger. The other one may have been a little smaller than this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you go on to claim that you were crammed in and as a result 20 people suffocated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I claim 1.000 per cent that there may have been even more than 20.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there some poisonous gas released there to choke you in there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't release any poisonous gas, but I had the impression that they started the central heating.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In order to choke you probably?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To torture us, to make us suffer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of building was it in Karakaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the workshop of the technical training centre, educational centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me, under those circumstances, crammed as you were and transported in that way and put up in that way, how did you manage to count 750 under those circumstances? How did you manage to count how many of you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't count, sir, but just like that, amongst ourselves, we were making a rough estimate that there were about 700 of us, and that proved to be correct later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did that prove to be correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After lists were made of the people captured.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you're talking about people executed. Do you know whether the bodies of those executed men were found, how many bodies were found, how many were established were to have been killed? From what you have said, how many of those were found and confirmed as having been killed in the incident you are testifying about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not a single was found, but, sir, there are families who came to report to the Red Cross in Tuzla, and you can get the necessary documentation to see how many people were killed, and not a single one has been found up to this point.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, and Mr. Nice is examining a witness for a crime of which not a single victim has been exhumed or discovered or of which there is no forensic evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We've got his evidence of what happened. Now, have you got any more questions you want to ask him?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do, of course. You gave me an hour and a half, so the least I can do is make use of it. And I hope you will give me some additional time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I add something? I omitted to say something, sir. May I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What Mr. Milosevic asked about whether any bodies had been found, I had forgotten to mention that it is true that some were found, but I don't know exactly how many. I forgot that. But some were found. I just don't know how many.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From a list of 64 men, you gave the names of four, and you don't know even the names of the rest. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You -- as you asked me yourself, I was working in Belgrade. But I knew the people from my village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You listed the names of four men.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, we can't hear the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you can't identify them, nor can you claim how many people were killed there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could list 60-odd names. There's a list here of people from my village, then people killed from Klisa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the bodies of those killed from Klisa and from your village were not found, were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: True. From my village, they were not found, but some were found that were from Klisa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they don't know under what circumstances they lost their lives. What is it during the war? Were they members of BH army ranks or were they executed? You yourself don't know where they are.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bodies of people that were found were executed in Karakaj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you then, as you say that you amongst yourselves, talking amongst yourselves, crammed as you were to such an extent that 20 people suffocated to death you found out how many of you were there, exactly that figure, that number of you were brought there? Were the reasons why you knew how many were brought there this testimony of yours today, or do you have some other logical reason to give as to how you knew exactly how many of you were there though you were able to communicate only with the three or four men immediately next to you as you were so crammed in there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I knew exactly how many people had been captured from my village, and the other people also knew for their own villages how many people had been captured. So it wasn't difficult to add up the figures like two and two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I am not very good at that kind of arithmetic, but as you say that on the first night 20 people choked to death in the room that you were in and that later on a relative of yours, I won't say in public session how he's related to you, you gave his name, that among those 20 there were two men that you name, how is it possible that you didn't see the two of them that suffocated but you -- you were told about them by this relative subsequently? How come you yourself didn't see them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew those two very well, but I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that's why I'm asking you. As you say you saw these men who had suffocated from this pressure and lack of space later, and you are now confirming that you knew them well, but you didn't see them. How is it possible that you saw them, saw those that choked but you didn't see the two that you knew so well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point in time, I just couldn't look at the bodies. It made me sick to look at them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. 1098. You claim on page 5, fourth paragraph, that in four days in Karakaj, the Serbs, as you say, killed 160 men and that you remember the names of only five of this figure of 160, that you don't remember the names of the rest because you left the area when you were 17 and went to Belgrade; is that right? That's what you confirmed a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During those five days, I am claiming to this very day I don't wish to say that I am a hundred per cent sure of the figure, but 50 or 51 people from Trsic were captured, and the same man from Trsic killed all the people from Trsic while they were in Karakaj. So there were 50 of them alone. What about those other 20? Then another 25, they allegedly drove to Sarajevo to be exchanged and those that were taken out four at a time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you worked it out. So you said people from Trsic who were captured. Was there fighting? Was there a battle in Trsic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They also fled to Klisa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether there was fighting, combat in Trsic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I'm unable to say. That's quite a way from me.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry, we didn't hear the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't hear anything about fighting in Trsic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that is far away from me, 15 kilometres away. How can I know what is going on over there?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you said that 50 people were Trsic were captured. Were they civilians who were captured, those 50 people from Trsic or were they captured in fighting against Serb forces? Are you claiming that they were captured civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. In view of the fact that the killed were taken out on different days, sometimes in groups of two or three, sometimes individually, what kind of arithmetic did you use to reach this figure of 160? What you explained a moment ago, how many people were captured in Trsic and then there are 20 more or 30 more, how are you claiming all these things, on what basis?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because when they took us off to Pilica in Drinatrans buses, we had been almost halved or, rather, a third had been killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know because when they drove us to Pilica and shut us up there, so many people were missing. One-third were missing right away, even more than a third.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps they took them off in some other direction. They just weren't with you. You don't know what really happened to them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I could go back and have that sketch again so I can explain some things to Mr. Milosevic, where they were killed, how they were killed, how they were taken out, and how many of them were killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness have his sketch. Or at least put it on the Sanction may be the best way to deal with it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Milosevic, the room marked with the number 3 and the letter "A" and you see this kind of fence, they took people to the previous room where there was 700-odd of us, and then from there they called people out and took off the wealthier ones, people who had the coffee bars, shops, businessmen, they took them out first killing them and demanding money and jewellery from them. Every day this happened several times a day. So it wasn't hard to count if you want to know. It wasn't hard too count.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how did you count them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1455 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't count them all. I didn't even know that I would survive. It didn't interest me that much. All I know is that when we got to Pilica so many were missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Private session or redact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Redact. Yes. A few questions more and we're going to adjourn, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're still in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And Your Honour, before he resumes with these questions may I make this observation. I don't want to deprive myself of the forensic flourishes that come in re-examination but the Chamber might want to know, may want to have the advantage of considering over night that this witness made a statement about these events five days after the incident he's telling about. utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. You've got about two minutes left and then we'll adjourn, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.text: So regarding those four days, you know five names of the people killed, and on the other hand, among the 24 guards or soldiers who are whatever you want to call them, Serbs, you knew as many as four, is that right, by name?
